It all starts off with a huge divisional matchup in the early window. Detroit will host Chicago in a heavyweight showdown that could end up deciding the NFC North champion later this season. Both teams will enter this matchup at 8-2 and have faced very little resistance in recent weeks. As such, this will be a huge measuring stick game that reveals just how good each team is before the final stretch of the regular season. This matchup looks to be a football feast that should provide something for everyone. Ben Johnson vs. Dan Campbell is always appointment television. Detroit and Chicago have elite offenses and defensive units that are just coming into form. And all of this is on top of the historic rivalry between the two franchises. So which team will gain bragging rights this year? And will the winning team eventually win the division title? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Here are three bold predictions ahead of this massive NFC North showdown on Thanksgiving. Jared Goff , Caleb Williams continue recent struggles on Thanksgiving Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Everyone knows that Detroit and Chicago have two of the best offenses in the NFL in 2026. That said, neither team is immune from being a little bit off their game. What happens if both teams stumble out of the gates? This is more likely to happen than it might seem on the surface. Caleb has struggled in recent weeks , throwing for just 460 passing yards with four touchdowns and five interceptions in the past two games. Goff has been much more reliable, but he's even thrown all four of his 2026 interceptions over the past four games. It's important to note that these recent struggles haven't exactly come against elite competition. So what happens when these two juggernauts face off after a very short week of rest? Conventional wisdom suggests that stopping the run should be a priority for both teams. But given each quarterback's recent penchant for turnovers, both Detroit and Chicago may emphasize being opportunistic on defense instead. And if that happens, this game could become downright sloppy. Goff and Williams will combine for 400 or fewer passing yards on Thanksgiving. On top of that, they will commit a combined four turnovers, with at least two of them being interceptions. Will this game turn into a low-scoring trainwreck with neither offense able to get into gear? Lions, Bears compete to see who has the better run game instead Fortunately, the Bears and Lions each have elite running games to make up the difference. It is no secret that each team will look to establish the run, but that won't make a difference. This game will quickly turn into good old-fashioned trench warfare with the running game deciding the contest. Here's the prediction: both teams will combine for more rushing yards than passing yards in this game. If Detroit and Chicago do end up with 400 combined passing yards, that means they'd need to average 200 rushing yards for this bold prediction to hit. How likely is that to happen? Based on their track records this season, it is unlikely but certainly possible. The Lions only have one game in 2026 with over 200 rushing yards. Detroit put up 230 yards against Minnesota back on November 1st. Meanwhile, Chicago has two 200+ rushing yard games this season. The Bears ripped off 291 rushing yards in Week 1 while demolishing the Panthers. They followed that up with 232 yards a few weeks later against the Jets. Make sure to start Jahmyr Gibbs and D'Andre Swift in fantasy football just in case. Detroit wins a low-scoring slugfest with Chicago, capturing lead in NFC North standings Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images It is difficult to overstate the importance of this game for both teams. Neither team's chances of making the playoffs will be too badly bruised by losing this one. However, gaining a divisional loss would be bad news for either team. It would be especially catastrophic for Chicago after starting 0-2 in NFC North games . Plus neither team wants to set up the opportunity to be swept and potentially lose a division title because of a head-to-head tiebreaker. With both teams so evenly matched, the outcome of this game may end up coming down to home field advantage. The Lions come out on top in this one in similar fashion to some of their most iconic wins in recent seasons. Detroit will possess the ball last, drain the rest of the clock, and deliver a game-winning score only if absolutely necessary. If these predictions come true, this game may not become the shootout that some fans want to watch. Instead, it will set up a potential high-scoring rematch in January with a lot on the line. This Thursday, they'll host the Chicago Bears, who also enter this game at 8-2, but are 0-2 in the division, putting them in second place. Despite the Lions' better record and the game being at Ford Field in downtown Detroit, the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions +2.5 points . In Ben Johnson's first year as head coach, the Bears went 11-6 and won the NFC North. They beat the Packers in the Wild Card but lost to the Rams in the Divisional round, ending a season that exceeded expectations. This offseason, the Bears made a few tweaks to their offense while overhauling half of their defense. On offense, priority No. 1 was replacing their center, Drew Dalman, who surprisingly retired. So the Bears traded with the Patriots for Garrett Bradbury, then drafted Iowa's Logan Jones in the second round. At receiver, they traded away DJ Moore and replaced him with former Lion Kalif Raymond, who has stepped into a starting role in the slot and flashed. On defense, the Bears lost all four of their top safeties (Kevin Byard, Jaquan Brisker, Jonathan Owens, and Chauncey Gardner-Johnson), their top linebacker in Tremaine Edmunds, starting NT Andrew Billings, and EDGE Dominique Robinson. At safety, the Bears made two splash moves: drafting Dillon Thieneman in the first round and signing Coby Bryant in free agency, who unfortunately suffered a season-ending injury, but they also signed Cam Lewis, who has since stepped into a starting role. Former Michigan Wolverine Devin Bush was signed in free agency to fill an Edmunds-sized void at linebacker, and Neville Gallimore was brought in to start at nose tackle. When Gallimore struggled, Chicago made a significant in-season trade, sending two first-round picks to acquire NT Jeffery Simmons. The Bears opened the season by dropping 59 points on the Panthers and had Johnson talking about setting the NFL scoring record . The next week, the Bears scored only three points in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings. Wins over the Eagles and Jets helped them regain rhythm, but they fell to the Packers in Week 5—their third consecutive loss to an NFC North rival dating back to last season when they lost to the Lions in Week 18. Since their 3-2 start to the season, the Bears have been on a roll, winning their last five games, rolling up over 30 points on the Falcons (31-23), Patriots (30-24), and Seahawks (34-17), but they have shown some kinks in the armor of late. Quarterback Caleb Williams was lucky to overcome a four-interception performance in Week 9 to beat the Bucs 27-24, and this past Sunday, he underwhelmed again , but Chicago's defense delivered, and the Bears beat the Saints 21-13. Tech couple Anthony Barr Picks Bears To Win NFC North Over Lions Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports Dallin Ballard · Gameday Chitown Fri, November 20, 2026 at 12:45 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North race has narrowed down to two teams, and former Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr believes the Chicago Bears are the ones to beat, according to Yahoo Sports . On "The Jim Rome Show," during a Nov. 16 appearance, Barr clarified that the division title depends on a fight between Chicago and Minnesota. He dismissed the Detroit Lions as a long-term threat despite their current standing at the top of the table. Barr pointed to a specific injury that could sink Detroit's season. For the Lions' defense, it was distressing to witness Aidan Hutchinson's awful injury, according to him. That unit is already taking a hit after struggles over the last two or three years. With Hutchinson out, the Lions lack the defensive anchor needed to close out a tight division race. The Defensive Edge Chicago has a clear path to the top spot because of its improved defensive line. The defensive line's addition of Jeffery Simmons has proven huge, Barr pointed out. This move helps the pass rush and could mask issues in the secondary. While some fans worry about the back end of the defense, Simmons brings a physical presence that changes how offenses attack the Bears. The offense under head coach Ben Johnson is also playing better football right now. Throughout the season, the chemistry and camaraderie between Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams have become evident, Barr observed. They have proven they can score points and move the ball effectively. This balance makes them a dangerous opponent for anyone in the conference. Why the Packers Are Out Green Bay is not part of this conversation, according to Barr. Packers defense still leaves much to be desired, he believes, and they lack any running game. Without a ground attack, the offense cannot control the clock or keep the defense fresh. This inconsistency puts them behind both Chicago and Minnesota in the standings. The Vikings remain a strong contender with the number one defense in the league. Kirk Cousins has given them a breath of fresh air after offensive struggles with previous quarterbacks. However, Barr sees the Bears as the team with the most momentum heading into the final stretch of the season. The division outcome will probably hinge on the two remaining games played between the Bears and Lions. The teams face off on Thanksgiving and then again in their Week 17 showdown in Chicago. The division could be at stake in that final matchup on Jan. 10, 2027, serving as the regular season's last game.

away.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). According to the NFL transaction wire, the Eagles claimed offensive tackle Ajani Cornelius off waivers. The Cowboys waived the tackle Tuesday. Standing taller than 6-foot-4 and 310 pounds, Cornelius went off the NFL draft board to Dallas at No. 204 overall in the sixth round during 2025. NFL.com's Lance Zierlein praised Cornelius for his college experience and size but questioned his technique. "A durable lineman with NFL traits and four years of starting experience, Cornelius lacks standout flashes on tape. He has been a full-time right tackle but lacks protection talent to stay outside as a pro," wrote NFL.com's Lance Zierlein during the 2025 draft process. "He has access to physical tools but needs to play with better bend and hand quickness to help stabilize his play." In four regular season games, he didn't receive an offensive snap with the Cowboys. At his best, that's what proved to be with the Cowboys. "He can cover up defenders with size but is frequently out-leveraged at the point of attack," Zierlein added . "His average body control and slide quickness should be mitigated in smaller spaces but those issues will still be concerning against explosive interior rushers. "The traits should make him a Day 3 target, but his ceiling might be as a backup." Even a backup role with the Cowboys, though, was difficult for Cornelius to find. On Thursday, he returns to Arlington, Texas, for a Thanksgiving Day contest against his former team as the starting quarterback for the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles. "Just going to go play another football game," Milton said of the holiday reunion. "I mean, obviously, I was just there a month ago, but I mean, it's going to be a great game. ... Milton is coming off his first career NFL win. He helped the Eagles (3-7) snap a seven-game losing streak with a wire-to-wire 19-16 victory Sunday against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers. Philadelphia signed Milton to the 53-man roster off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16 after quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots. Originally a sixth-round pick by New England in 2024, Milton replaced Tanner McKee and made his first NFL start in a Week 9 loss to the New York Giants. Milton will be making his first career road start when he faces the Cowboys (5-6), who are seeking a season sweep after beating McKee and the Eagles 38-21 on the road on "Monday Night Football" in Week 7. Dallas has not swept Philadelphia since the 2021 season. Dallas is playing its third consecutive home game and riding high after a 51-30 trouncing of the Tennessee Titans in Week 11. Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and rushed for a score in the Cowboys' first 50-point outburst since 2022.
